Study hour (150h)
= 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
chung.Description: Perspective is a subject that helps students draw third dimention objects on a flat surface like the image when we look at the object in real life. Perspective drawing is concerned with achieving a sense of space, of depth and of the third dimension, within the limits of the flat drawing surface. Students can use the rules of perspective in sketching, finding ideas and creativity in designing.For those concerned with freehand perspective is provided all the important printciples, insights and "shortcuts" necessary for effective drawing and life sketching. Essentially, perspective drawing deals with this appearance of things, i.e., with how three dimensional reality "look" and how it is best drawn on two dimensional surface as a canvas, sketch pad, or illustration board.

Understand How we see for perspective drawing and Why appearance differs from reality theory, concept of Picture plane, Cone of Vision. Understand concept of Vanishing points and eyes level, how to find vanishing point, eyes level on the picture plane, vanishing point of specical lines.

Take photographs, find and analyze the perspective elements in the photographs, like vanishing point, eyes level, vanishing point of specical lines. Explain why appearance differs from reality theory.

- Knowledge: Understand the basic rules, concept of perspective. Understand why appearance differs from reality theory, understand concept of Vanishing points and eyes level, how to find vanishing point, eyes level on the picture plane, vanishing point of specical lines.
- Skills: Analyze pictures for perspective fundamentals and basic concepts

1. Students take a number of photographs following instruction in the area. Students may use AI generated pictures or existing pictures for reference. Discuss with the instrcutor about the relevance of the photographs taken.
2. Students choose suitable pictures and analyze the perspective elements in the photographs, edit and highline the perspective elements using digital drawing tools like Adobe Illustrator.
3. Combine unedited and edited pictures into a report.

Submission Files:
- Final document including the original photographs, analyzed photographs, and additional analysis if needed.
- Original drawing files if required (PDF).
In-class work:
- Peer and instructor feedback on photographs and analysis drawing.
Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions
